title: Zero Conditional: If + Present, Present
grammarNote:
Нулевой условный (Zero Conditional) — для научных фактов и вещей, которые ВСЕГДА происходят при определённом условии. Стопроцентная уверенность.

📌 Формула: IF + Present Simple → Present Simple
(оба глагола в Present Simple — не будущее время!)

① Научные факты:
   "If you heat water to 100°C, it boils." (всегда!)
   "If you mix red and blue, you get purple."

② Общие истины:
   "If students miss classes, their grades suffer."
   "If you don't sleep enough, you feel tired."

③ Инструкции:
   "If the printer breaks, call IT support."

💡 Можно заменить IF на WHEN — смысл не меняется:
"When you heat water to 100°C, it boils." = то же самое

⚠️ Отличие от 1st Conditional:
Zero: "If it rains, the ground gets wet." (всегда!)
1st: "If it rains, I will stay home." (конкретная возможная ситуация)

grammarTip:
Нулевой условный — запомни три вещи:

① IF + Present Simple, Present Simple (нет "will"!):
❌ "If you heat water, it will boil." → это 1st Conditional
✅ "If you heat water, it boils." → Zero Conditional

② IF = WHEN (взаимозаменяемы):
"If you press this button, the light turns on." = "When you press..."

③ Только для ФАКТОВ (100% уверенность):
"If babies are hungry, they cry." (закон природы)
"If you don't water plants, they die." (всегда!)

exercises.hint: Zero conditional: result clause = present simple, NOT will.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct negative form.
exercises.text: If you ___ (not study), you fail the test.
exercises.hint: If-clause in zero conditional: present simple negative = don't + base verb.

opts: If it rains, I will stay home.
If it rains, I stay home.
If it will rain, I stay home.
If it rained, I stayed home.
exercises.correct: If it rains, I stay home.
exercises.hint: Zero conditional: both clauses use present simple. "will" = first conditional.

exercises.text: Plants die if they ___ (not get) enough sunlight.
exercises.hint: If-clause after the result clause: present simple negative.

exercises.text: If you mix yellow and blue, you ___ green.
exercises.hint: Scientific fact = zero conditional. Result: present simple.

exercises.text: Zero conditional uses "will" in the result clause.
exercises.hint: False — zero conditional uses present simple in BOTH clauses. "will" belongs to first conditional.

exercises.text: If I drink too much coffee, I ___ (not sleep) well.
exercises.hint: Result clause of zero conditional: present simple negative.

exercises.text: "When" can replace "if" in a zero conditional when:
opts: the event is a real future plan
we are talking about the past
exercises.hint: "When" replaces "if" only for guaranteed, repeated events — not future possibilities.

exercises.instruction: Find the sentence with if-clause second.
exercises.text: Which sentence has the "if" clause second?
opts: The ground gets wet if it rains.
If it rains, the ground gets wet.
If the ground is wet, it rained.
It rained if the ground was wet.
exercises.correct: The ground gets wet if it rains.
exercises.hint: When if-clause comes second, no comma is needed between the clauses.
"If" or "when" — both correct here. "When" emphasises it always happens; "if" introduces the condition.

exercises.text: If students ___ every day, their English improves.
exercises.hint: If-clause of zero conditional: present simple → practise (no -s for they).

exercises.text: Zero conditional can describe personal habits and routines.
exercises.hint: True — zero conditional covers both universal facts and regular personal habits.

questions.text: Zero conditional uses ___ in both clauses.
questions.hint: Both the if-clause and the result clause use present simple.

questions.text: If you ___ (exercise) regularly, you stay healthy.
questions.hint: Zero conditional: if + present simple, present simple.

questions.text: If glass breaks, the pieces ___ sharp.
questions.hint: Zero conditional result clause: present simple.

questions.text: "If it rains, I will stay home" is a zero conditional.
questions.hint: "will stay" = first conditional, not zero. Zero uses present simple in both clauses.

opts: If you heat it, it will melt.
If you heat it, it melts.
If you will heat it, it melts.
If you heated it, it melts.
questions.correct: If you heat it, it melts.
questions.hint: Zero conditional: if + present simple, present simple.

questions.text: Plants ___ (die) if they don't get sunlight.
questions.hint: Result clause in zero conditional: present simple.

questions.text: Can "when" replace "if" in a zero conditional?
opts: Yes, when the event always happens
questions.correct: Yes, when the event always happens
questions.hint: "When" replaces "if" when the event is a guaranteed, repeated occurrence.

questions.text: If you mix red and blue, you ___ purple.
questions.hint: Zero conditional — result clause uses present simple: get.

questions.text: Which example is NOT a zero conditional?
opts: If I eat late, I feel ill.
If you press play, music starts.
If she studies, she will pass.
questions.correct: If she studies, she will pass.

questions.text: Zero conditional describes scientific and universal truths.
questions.hint: Yes — zero conditional is for facts, laws, and things that always happen.

questions.text: What does Kamila's mother say about her planning style?
opts: She is very careful — she makes plans not promises
questions.correct: She is very careful — she makes plans not promises
questions.hint: Paragraph 3: "You are very careful. You don't make promises — you make plans."

questions.text: Amir makes detailed written plans every week like Kamila.
questions.hint: Amir acts immediately — he doesn't wait or write plans.

questions.correct: A requirement that must be met
questions.hint: A condition is something that must be true or done for something else to happen.
